- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods, especially when sentiment is positive and rising; reduce forecast peaks when sentiment is weak or negative.
- Underestimate prices after strong upward spikes; model tends to overreact and then overshoot, so cap or dampen forecast peaks after sentiment spikes.
- When sentiment is consistently negative or volatile, reduce forecast magnitude and avoid sharp upward revisions.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 10-day average, adjust downward; if below, adjust upward — especially if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive, then underestimates later days — adjust for lagged sentiment decay.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast magnitude in response to negative sentiment trends.
